Unified Memory (UM) represents a fundamental architectural shift in how computing resources are managed, particularly within the context of Apple’s silicon ecosystem (M-series chips) and increasingly relevant in heterogeneous computing environments involving CPUs and GPUs. To understand how it enables local AI workstations to run models larger than conventional discrete GPU memory limits, we must first dissect the traditional bottleneck: the strict separation of host memory (CPU RAM) and device memory (GPU VRAM).

In a conventional PC architecture with a discrete NVIDIA or AMD GPU, the system operates on a "copy-based" model. The CPU holds the operating system, applications, and data in DDR4
